title: Warm Crisp Moroccan Lamb Kefta Tagine
description: A roasted and crispy Moroccan dish featuring lamb kefta, gouda cheese, and a sweet glaze, perfect for a comforting meal. This Buddhist-temple-friendly recipe is easy to make and delicious to eat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, combine the ground lamb, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper, and mix well with your hands until just combined.
Use your hands to shape the lamb mixture into small kefta, about 1 1/2 inches long and 1 inch in diameter.
Place the kefta on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving a little space between each kefta to allow for even cooking.
Drizzle the olive oil over the kefta and gently roll them to coat evenly.
Roast the kefta in the preheated oven for 18 minutes, or until cooked through and lightly browned on the outside.
While the kefta are cooking, mix the honey and garlic in a small bowl until well combined.
After the kefta have roasted for 15 minutes, brush the honey glaze all over them and continue to roast for the remaining 3 minutes.
Remove the kefta from the oven and sprinkle the shredded gouda cheese over the top of each kefta.
Return the kefta to the oven and cook for an additional 2 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove the kefta from the oven and sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley.
